scope: synthetic orchestration benchmark and Qubes fleet sizing only; no production worker or mission mutation semantics changed
problem: The finite-fleet benchmark could score one topology at a time, but choosing a Qubes layout was still manual. That risks selecting a resource-heavy layout or a fast fused layout that violates capability isolation requirements.

independent_reviews.reason: Evaluate the same runtime DAG across explicit candidate layouts, apply the same readiness thresholds to every candidate, and rank only layouts that satisfy the full gate. This turns topology selection into reproducible evidence rather than manual interpretation.

Reject candidate workers that co-reside forbidden capability pairs before latency can make the layout look attractive. Invalid or capability-incomplete layouts remain in results as ineligible evidence rather than silently disappearing.

independent_reviews.preferred: offline bounded search over explicit candidates
independent_reviews.reason: Adds zero qrexec traffic and zero production processes. Ranking prioritizes constrained latency, then fewer workers, then lower queue delay. maxTopologies bounds CPU/memory use and prevents accidental combinatorial search.

approaches.name: manual-topology-comparison
approaches.correctness: can be correct when reviewed carefully but is easy to make inconsistent across runs
approaches.robustness: weak against omitted layouts or inconsistent thresholds
approaches.regression_risk: medium because deployment choices are not executable QA

approaches.name: automatic-unbounded-partition-search
approaches.robustness: requires a much richer trust/capability policy model
approaches.latency: can become combinatorial as capability count grows
approaches.regression_risk: higher due to large search/state surface

approaches.name: bounded-trust-aware-worker-fleet-topology-evaluator
approaches.correctness: scores explicit 1/2/3/4-worker candidates against the actual runtime DAG and uniform readiness thresholds
approaches.robustness: fail-closed on duplicate topology IDs, invalid bounds, impossible capability coverage, and forbidden capability co-residency
approaches.latency: offline only and bounded by maxTopologies
approaches.resources: small in-memory maps/arrays; no VM or transport use
approaches.regression_risk: low because MissionQueue, coordinator, qrexec, and worker runtime semantics are unchanged

current_fixture_result.expectedWinner: two-worker-fused when coder+qa co-residency is allowed

controls.isolatedFourWorker: 210ms-equivalent and remains eligible but loses resource tie-break to safe two-worker layout

trust_boundary_rule: Capability co-residency must be policy-driven. The evaluator accepts forbiddenCapabilityPairs and excludes a fused topology before ranking if a worker contains a forbidden pair.

required: two-worker fused topology preserves 210ms-equivalent critical path when policy permits it
one-worker control measures 290ms-equivalent and fails strict speedup readiness
four-worker independent topology remains a valid zero-penalty fallback
forbidden coder+qa co-residency rejects the fused topology and selects the isolated layout
duplicate topology IDs and topology counts over maxTopologies fail closed
existing graph and single-fleet benchmarks remain unchanged
qa.release_note: Hosted GitHub runner provisioning remains a separate blocker. These tests are part of the existing orchestration benchmark suite but do not replace independent hosted CI or real Qubes qualification.

failure_lessons: The fastest topology is not automatically the safest topology; trust boundaries must be evaluated before latency ranking.
Four workers are not necessary for this fixture when coordination/coder/QA co-residency is permitted; two workers preserve the same critical path with a smaller Qube/RAM footprint.
A single shared specialist worker destroys the expected fan-out speedup even when the DAG itself is parallel.
Keep topology search bounded and explicit until real Qubes measurements justify a more complex optimizer.
